title: REITs vs. REIT Mutual Funds: A Practical Guide for Indian Investors
description: Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) allow direct investment in income-generating properties, offering rental income and potential capital appreciation. REIT.

faq.q: What is the minimum investment for REITs and REIT mutual funds?
faq.a: For direct REITs, the minimum investment was initially ₹50,000, later reduced to ₹10,000-₹15,000 per unit for some issues. For REIT mutual funds, you can start with as little as ₹500 via SIPs or ₹5,000 for lumpsum investments, similar to other mutual funds.

faq.q: Are REITs and REIT mutual funds suitable for NRIs?
faq.a: Yes, NRIs can invest in both Indian REITs and REIT mutual funds, subject to FEMA regulations. They typically need an NRO or NRE account and a demat account for direct REITs.

Direct REIT units are traded on stock exchanges, offering liquidity, though it can vary based on the specific REIT. REIT mutual fund units can be redeemed with the fund house, typically settled within a few business days.
No, like any market-linked investment, REITs do not guarantee returns. Returns depend on property performance, rental income, market conditions, and capital appreciation.

faq.q: What is the role of SEBI in regulating REITs?
faq.a: SEBI regulates REITs in India, setting guidelines for their structure, investments, disclosures, and governance to protect investor interests.

faq.q: Can I invest in global REITs from India?
faq.a: Yes, some Indian mutual funds offer schemes that invest in global REITs, providing exposure to international real estate markets. These are typically fund-of-funds or feeder funds.

faq.q: What is the difference between an InvIT and a REIT?
faq.a: While both are trust structures, REITs invest in income-generating real estate assets, whereas InvITs invest in infrastructure assets like roads, power lines, and pipelines. Both are regulated by SEBI.
